name: Sensfrx.ai (SFX) – Fraud Prevention & Card Testing Protection for WooCommerce
author: sensfrx

sections.description:
WooCommerce fraud prevention built around what store owners actually lose money on: card-testing bots, fake orders and fake accounts, stolen-card orders, AI agents used for fraud, and chargebacks you lose even with proof.

We read 245 merchant threads on Reddit and store-owner forums before building it. The most common complaints were chargebacks lost despite proof, card-testing bots and fake accounts. Each section below starts with one of them.

Sensfrx gives every order, sign-up and login on your store a fraud risk score from 0 to 100, with the reasons in plain words. Clear fraud is refused before the payment is taken. Orders in the gray zone wait for your decision. Real customers check out as before.

The problems it solves

“I’m getting hundreds of card-testing attempts and CAPTCHA doesn’t stop them.”
Card-testing bots skip your storefront and hit the checkout directly, so CAPTCHA never sees them. Sensfrx watches the payments themselves: after repeated declines from one browser, network or delivery address, checkout is refused before another order or charge is created. It covers the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page. During an attack, checkout needs a real browser session; returning customers are not affected.

“Thousands of fake accounts, and my email tool bills me for every one.”
Scripted sign-ups, throwaway email addresses and accounts made in bulk from one device or network are caught at sign-up. Addresses Sensfrx judged fake are kept out of MailPoet, Mailchimp for WooCommerce, Klaviyo, Omnisend, CartFlows and Abandoned Cart Lite, so you stop paying for bot contacts and your abandoned-cart emails stop hurting your sender reputation.

“The order looks risky. Do I ship it or cancel it?”
You get a score with the reasons, not just a label: “4 cards tried in 18 minutes”, “Ships to a parcel forwarder”, “Card used by 3 other customers”. Risky orders go on hold in one Fraud review list, highest risk first, and you approve or cancel in one click.

“I lost the chargeback even though I had proof.”
When an order is disputed as fraud, Sensfrx lists the customer’s earlier undisputed orders from your store that share the same device, IP address or account, and checks them against the Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0, Mastercard and American Express rules. Print it or save it as PDF and attach it to your reply. Customers with an earlier fraud dispute at your store are flagged before you ship again.

“Stolen-card orders keep shipping.”
Every order is scored before you fulfill it, using signals merchants trust: several cards tried on one account, a card shared across customers, many customers ordering from one device, a parcel forwarder. Address (AVS) and security-code (CVV) results from Stripe, Braintree, Square, Authorize.Net, PayPal and other gateways are part of the score.

“I’m paying fees on orders I cancel as fraud.”
Clear fraud is refused before the payment is taken, so there is nothing to refund and no fee kept on a cancelled order.

“AI agents are browsing and checking out on my store. Which ones are fraud?”
AI agents can now browse, sign up and check out like a person, and fraudsters use the same tools to run stolen cards, create accounts and claim coupons at scale. Sensfrx flags sessions that click, move and pause like an AI agent or a scripted browser, and checkouts driven by automation tools such as Playwright, Selenium and Puppeteer. A request that claims to be a known agent, such as ChatGPT’s or Google’s, but fails the proof (a wrong or reused signature, or an address outside the operator’s published ranges) is caught as an impersonator. Agents that prove who they are are labeled “Verified AI agent”, but they are not trusted more: every other check still runs.

Also included

  • Fraud intelligence: every check with its reason. Search by email, IP address or order, filter by risk and export to CSV.
  • 74 fraud rules you control: set the score or action for each, and keep your own block and allow lists by IP address, email, user ID or username.
  • Account protection: logins and password resets from a new device, an unusual network or an impossible location are challenged.

Why store owners trust it

  • Free to start. The Free plan includes 500 checks a month. You add a card to activate it, and the Free plan is not charged.
  • Your checkout never waits on us. If Sensfrx does not answer in time, the order goes through and is marked as not checked.
  • No emails to your customers. Sensfrx never emails your shoppers. Confirmation emails, if you switch them on, go out from your store’s own address.
  • No card data. Card numbers are never sent to Sensfrx.
  • Independently audited. Sensfrx security controls are audited to SOC 2 Type II.

Set up in a minute

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Sensfrx, enter your email and the 6-digit code we send you. No API keys to copy.
  3. Orders, sign-ups and logins are scored from that moment.

“I was being attacked by bots trying to create accounts, but they were very supportive and helpful. I ended up switching to a paid plan because there were so many attacks, but it was worth it. I plan to continue using them.”
Shohei Tanaka, store owner

Privacy & External Services

Important: This plugin connects to Sensfrx.ai (SFX)’s external fraud detection API to provide real-time fraud analysis. When the plugin is active and your store is connected, the following data may be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai servers for fraud detection purposes:

Data Transmitted:

  • User IP addresses and device fingerprints
  • Registration information (email addresses, usernames, registration timestamps)
  • Login attempts, timestamps, and authentication events
  • Transaction details (order amounts, product information, payment methods)
  • User profile updates and password change events
  • Billing and shipping addresses
  • WooCommerce order metadata

External Services Used:

  • Sensfrx.ai (SFX) API: https://sensfrx.ai
  • Privacy Policy: https://sensfrx.ai/privacy-policy
  • Terms of Service: https://sensfrx.ai/terms
  • Trust & Security: https://sensfrx.ai/trust

User Consent & Configuration:

By connecting your store (with your email and a one-time code, or with a Property ID and Property Secret from https://client.sensfrx.ai), you acknowledge that user data will be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai’s servers for fraud analysis. The plugin will not transmit any data until the store is connected.

Data Security:

Sensfrx.ai (SFX) security controls are independently audited (SOC 2 Type II). All data transmissions use HTTPS encryption. For complete details about data handling, retention policies, and your rights under GDPR and other privacy regulations, please review Sensfrx.ai’s Privacy Policy.

Account:

To use this plugin you need a Sensfrx.ai (SFX) account. The plugin creates one when you connect with your email, or you can sign up at https://client.sensfrx.ai/signup. The Free plan includes 500 checks a month; a card is needed to activate it and the Free plan is not charged.

Upgrade Your Store Security

Stop losing revenue to fraud and protect your WooCommerce store with AI-driven fraud detection today!

Get Started for FREE

Support

Join our community for real-time support and fraud prevention insights:

  • Discord: https://discord.gg/zGBGQdwT4r
  • Documentation: Sensfrx WooCommerce Plugin Guide
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for Sensfrx and click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Open Sensfrx in the admin menu and enter your email address.
  3. Enter the 6-digit code we email you. If you are new to Sensfrx, add a card when asked to activate your plan. The Free plan is not charged.
  4. That’s it. Orders, logins and sign-ups are checked from now on. Open Fraud protection to choose what is checked and who gets alerts.

Prefer API keys? Open Settings in the plugin and paste the Property ID and Property Secret from your Sensfrx dashboard.
sections.faq:
How do I stop card testing on WooCommerce?

Install Sensfrx and leave Order fraud protection on. After repeated declined payments from one browser, network or delivery address, checkout is refused before another order or charge is created. This works on the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page, where most card-testing bots attack.

Why doesn’t CAPTCHA stop card-testing bots?

Most card-testing bots never load your storefront page. They send orders straight to the checkout or payment endpoint, so a CAPTCHA on the page is never shown to them. Sensfrx looks at the payment attempts themselves, so it sees the attack wherever it comes from.

How do I stop fake accounts and spam registrations on WooCommerce?

Leave Check new sign-ups and Block bots on. Scripted sign-ups, throwaway email addresses and bulk accounts from one device or network are refused or held, and fake addresses are kept out of your email marketing tools.

How do I win a chargeback on WooCommerce?

Open the disputed order and click Dispute evidence in the Sensfrx box. It lists the customer’s earlier undisputed orders that share the same device, IP address or account, which is the evidence the Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0 rules ask for. No tool can guarantee the bank’s decision, but this is the evidence card networks accept for “it was the real customer”.

Does Sensfrx detect AI agents like ChatGPT’s agent?

Yes. Sessions that behave like an AI agent or a scripted browser are flagged, and requests that claim to be a known agent but fail its proof are caught as impersonators. Agents that prove who they are are labeled “Verified AI agent” and still go through every other check. To also watch API and integration traffic, switch on AI agent and API protection in Fraud protection.

Is there a free plan?

Yes. The Free plan includes 500 checks a month. You add a card to activate it, and the Free plan is not charged. When the month’s checks run out, your store keeps taking orders as usual; they are not checked until the next month or until you upgrade.

Will Sensfrx block my real customers?

Sensfrx refuses only clear fraud, such as card testing and automated checkouts. Orders in the gray zone are put on hold for you to approve or cancel, with the reasons shown. You can change the action and score of every rule, and allow-list customers you trust.

What happens if Sensfrx does not answer?

The order goes through. The Sensfrx box on the order says the order was not checked, so you know to look at it yourself. Sensfrx never stops your checkout because of its own outage.

Does Sensfrx email my customers?

No. When a customer needs to confirm a login, payment or sign-up, the email goes out from your store’s own email address, and only if you switch it on.

Which payment gateways does it work with?

All of them. Sensfrx scores the order, not the card. Address and security-code results are also read from Stripe, Braintree, Square, Authorize.Net, PayPal and other gateways that save them on the order.

Does it work with the block checkout?

Yes. Card-testing protection covers the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page.

How do I fight a chargeback?

Open the order and click Dispute evidence in the Sensfrx box. It lists the customer’s earlier orders from your store that match this one and were not disputed, and says whether they meet the Visa, Mastercard and American Express rules. Upload it with your reply to the payment provider.

What data does the plugin send?

Only what fraud checks need: IP address, device and browser signals, the email and username, and the order details. No card numbers are ever sent. See Privacy & External Services below and our Privacy Policy.

  • Fixed: Overview and Fraud intelligence use the same inclusive UTC calendar ranges. Seven days now requests seven dates, rather than eight; the correction also applies to longer periods.
  • Improved: filtered empty activity states describe the selected filters without implying the whole store has no risky activity.

3.11.9

  • Fixed: fraud history requests preserve their date filters, restoring order records in Fraud intelligence.
  • Fixed: unavailable activity feeds show a retryable error instead of missing orders, zero totals or sample fraud records. Stale responses and exports are guarded while loading.
  • Fixed: order values retain their own currency and decimal precision; blocked totals stay separate by currency, and merchant reviews remain distinct from original risk.

3.11.8

  • Fixed: activity badges use the recorded fraud decision, so email addresses and notification wording cannot turn ordinary activity into blocked orders. Held orders show Held for review.
  • Fixed: email activity is excluded from order filters and counts.
  • Improved: fraud intelligence table actions remain reachable at narrow widths and enlarged zoom; complete currency metrics remain readable.

3.11.7

  • Added: automatic order reassessment after temporary security-service failures. Checkout stays available while unchecked fulfillment and downloads wait for a completed check or merchant review.
  • Fixed: recovery respects merchant holds, existing approvals, closed orders and changes to order details.
  • Fixed: retries and queue failures stay visible, and unconfirmed payment reversals remain unresolved. Cash-on-delivery recovery does not mark unpaid orders paid.

3.11.6

  • Fixed: temporary service and network errors remain explicitly unchecked on the order screen, instead of appearing as completed low-risk assessments. Checkout remains available.

3.11.5

  • Fixed: Overview statistics and filtered reviews load correctly on stores using WordPress plain permalinks.
  • Fixed: approval counts refresh immediately after single or bulk order reviews.
  • Fixed: closed orders leave the review queue and cannot report a new approval. Commerce status sync preserves original risk, retries temporary failures and shows unresolved sync problems.
  • Fixed: approving an unpaid on-hold order requests payment instead of marking it paid, even after its old fraud hold was removed.
  • Fixed: wrong sign-in codes no longer restart the ten-minute expiry. A code with an expired or unknown deadline requires a fresh sign-in.

3.11.4

  • Improved: Overview refreshes approval counts after review and describes approvals without claiming completed sales.
  • Fixed: repeated review approvals cannot mark an unpaid order as paid, revive closed orders or resend the same review email. Completed orders retain their status.
  • Fixed: bulk review accepts the transaction format returned by the SDK.
  • Fixed: background guest payment checks work without a shopper session.
  • Fixed: background payment confirmations are assessed without requiring the shopper to return to the thank-you page, using the order owner rather than an active admin session.
  • Fixed: bot requests are assessed even when browser device data is absent.
  • Fixed: challenged comments are saved in moderation, and comment decisions apply even when their severity label differs.
  • Fixed: a queued forced logout applies before page output and cannot show its blocked-account notice to another visitor.

  • Fixed: the order panel shows your approval or refusal while retaining the original risk details.

  • Fixed: WordPress password reset and registration confirmation messages remain visible.

  • Fixed: custom order lines and orders with deleted products still receive fraud checks instead of crashing.
  • Fixed: signed callbacks use the correct REST address on stores with plain permalinks. Existing callback registrations are repaired in the background without changing their signing secrets.
  • Fixed: review and refusal decisions are enforced even when a custom rule produces a different risk severity.
  • Fixed: an order awaiting security review cannot be paid from its payment link or retried checkout until the store approves it.
  • Improved: orders stopped before payment show the saved decision and reasons on the order screen.

3.11.3

  • Fixed: a customer you put on the allow list in Sensfrx could still be signed out, and sent a password reset, by the automated-browser check. That check now tells Sensfrx who is signed in, so your allow and block lists apply to it.
  • Fixed: a new Sensfrx account created from the plugin now uses your store’s time zone instead of India time.

3.11.2

  • Fixed: “Orders blocked” on the dashboard counted refused sign-ins and sign-ups as orders.
  • Fixed: order amounts in Fraud intelligence now show each order’s own currency. Totals add up orders in your store’s currency and count the others separately.
  • Fixed: the “Connect email” step showed as done on every WooCommerce store, even with no email setup.
  • Fixed: customer account alerts no longer show internal labels such as “Incident Triggered!” or “User Account Compromised”.
  • Fixed: the average risk score can no longer show above 100, guest order checks are logged as “before payment”, and the Fraud review message reads “Blocked”.
  • Changed: the Customer emails setting says plainly that these emails go out from your store’s own address.

3.11.1

  • Fixed: guest orders placed through the block checkout now send the shopper’s email, name and billing address to Sensfrx. Before, only the shipping address was sent, so email checks did not run on those orders and your dashboard showed the customer as Anonymous.
  • Fixed: the order amount sent to Sensfrx is now correct in every currency. Stores in euros, pounds, rupees and other currencies whose symbol is not “$” sent a wrong or empty amount for guest orders.
  • Fixed: connecting with your WordPress administrator email now sends a verification code, as for any other email. Before, it stopped with “The API did not respond correctly”.

3.11.0

  • New: each sign-in tells Sensfrx how the customer signed in (password, social sign-in such as Nextend Social Login, XML-RPC, or another method), so your Sensfrx dashboard shows it on logins and you can filter by it. Only whether a field was sent is checked, never its value. Sites with another sign-in plugin (passkeys, email links, single sign-on) can report it with the sensfrx_login_method filter.

3.10.1

  • Fixed: MailPoet could unsubscribe an existing subscriber whose address was kept out of email marketing, the next time their account was saved. Only new subscribers are now affected, and existing subscriptions are never changed.
  • Fixed: an address that belongs to an account on your store is never kept out because of a refused order, a refused checkout or a failed sign-up (anyone can type someone else’s address into a guest checkout).
  • Fixed: an order Sensfrx refused counts only once it is actually cancelled or failed, so nothing happens in shadow mode, for whitelisted customers, or while you keep the order open.
  • Checkouts refused during a card-testing attack are kept out for a week, each stored on its own, so an attack does not rewrite the list on every request.
  • Only rules with real weight count, and browser-integrity checks that privacy browsers trigger are no longer treated as signs of a fake account.

3.10.0

  • New: addresses Sensfrx judged fake stay out of your email marketing, so you are not billed for bot contacts and welcome and abandoned-cart emails do not go to junk addresses. This covers sign-ups Sensfrx allowed but that showed signs of a bot or a fake identity (for example a disposable address), orders Sensfrx refused, and checkouts refused during a card-testing attack. Such an address is saved as unsubscribed in MailPoet; Mailchimp for WooCommerce does not get its newsletter tick or the refused order; Klaviyo and Omnisend do not get the order or customer; Cart Abandonment Recovery (CartFlows) and Abandoned Cart Lite send it no abandoned-cart email. Nothing is deleted, nobody is emailed, and each new account kept out is listed in Activity. It lasts 90 days.
  • Developers can turn it off with the sensfrx_email_guard_enabled filter.
  • Sign-up checks now come with their reasons, as order checks do.

3.9.1

  • Fixed: the dispute evidence report no longer lists other guest customers’ orders as the customer’s own, and no longer counts shared or unknown IP addresses (fixed on the Sensfrx side; this release updates the order screen to match).
  • The dispute date is kept only when the payment provider supplies it (WooCommerce Stripe Gateway). A chargeback you report by hand no longer sets it, so the report counts card-network time limits conservatively instead of from the day you reported.
  • The report page runs in a sandbox in your browser.

3.9.0

  • New: dispute evidence. When a customer disputes an order as fraud, open “Dispute evidence” in the Sensfrx box on the order. It lists the customer’s earlier orders from your store that match this one (same account, device, IP address or delivery address) and were not disputed, and says whether they meet the card networks’ rules: Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0, Mastercard and American Express. Print it or save it as PDF and upload it with your reply to the payment provider.
  • The Sensfrx box now also appears on orders Sensfrx checked before version 3.7.0, with the dispute evidence link.
  • When a fraud dispute arrives through the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway, or you report one from the order page, its date is kept so the report counts earlier orders back from the day of the dispute.

3.8.1

  • Improved: card-testing protection is harder to get around and gentler on real customers.
  • Attack mode now starts only when most declined payments come from new visitors, so a payment-provider outage does not trigger it. New visitors share a limited allowance for at most two hours of an attack, and browsers first seen shortly before an attack count as new.
  • A delivery address is refused only when declines come from more than one browser or network, both address lines are used, and returning customers with a completed order are not affected.
  • Stores behind a CDN or proxy the plugin does not recognise are no longer treated as one visitor.
  • The pay-for-order page no longer counts a card form the payment method rejects before trying the card, and orders a shop manager marks as failed are not counted.
  • New: at most five “add payment method” attempts an hour per account, browser and network.
  • Declined payments are reported at the end of the request, with a limit per visitor; visitor hashes are removed from orders once they are settled.

3.8.0

  • New: protection against card testing (bots that run stolen card numbers through your checkout). After repeated declined payments from one browser or network, further attempts are refused before an order or payment is made, so no fee is paid on them. Declined payments to one delivery address under several different email addresses are stopped the same way.
  • New: when declined payments arrive from several visitors at once, checkout asks for a browser that has opened your cart or checkout page, which stops scripts that call the checkout directly. Returning customers are not affected.
  • New: declined payments are reported to Sensfrx, so an order placed out of a run of declines is held or refused.
  • Covers the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page. Shop managers are never limited. It follows the main “Fraud protection for this store” switch, and writes a line to the activity log when it acts.

3.7.1

  • Improved: when a customer finishes a sign-in with the emailed code, Sensfrx now learns that the device is theirs, so the same device is not asked for a code again for the same reason.
  • Improved: the plugin tells Sensfrx which version it is running, so support can see whether a store has the latest protections.

3.7.0

  • New: a Sensfrx box on the order screen. It shows what Sensfrx recommends for the order, what raised the risk in plain words, and anything that speaks for the shopper. It appears only on orders Sensfrx checked.
  • New: when Sensfrx holds or refuses an order, the order gets a private note that says why.
  • Improved: every reason in the review list has a plain name and a short explanation in place of a code.

3.6.5

  • Privacy: the one-way code sent in place of a typed username is now made with a random key that is created on your site and never leaves it, so nobody outside your store, Sensfrx included, can work out what was typed.
  • Fixed: the daily limit on emails to a customer now holds even when two requests arrive at the same instant.

3.6.4

  • Fixed: a customer could be unable to finish a sign-in for a day if their sign-in codes did not arrive, or if other emails to their address had used up the daily limit. Sign-in codes, confirmation links and your decisions on held orders are no longer held back by the daily limit, and a password reset makes new sign-in codes available straight away.
  • Fixed: if the store cannot send a sign-in code, the customer is told so instead of being asked for a code that never arrives, and the failure shows in the email log and setup notice.
  • Fixed: each held order now gets its own “approved” or “cancelled” email, even when one customer has two on the same day.
  • Improved: Sensfrx’s own refusals and sign-in code requests are no longer counted as failed passwords, and the activity log no longer records what was typed into the username box.

3.6.3

  • New: the setup checklist has a “Send customer emails from your store” step. It is ticked automatically when an SMTP plugin sends your store’s mail.
  • New: if WordPress cannot send Sensfrx’s emails to your customers (sign-in codes, order notices), Sensfrx shows one notice on its own screens and lets you know by email, at most once a week and only while emails are actually failing. It stops as soon as your mail works.

3.6.2

  • Improved: fewer emails to your customers. Sensfrx emails go out through your store’s own mail, so every unnecessary one costs your store’s sending reputation. Each customer now gets at most one email of the same kind a day (for example one “sign-in blocked” notice, however many attempts were blocked), at most three sign-in codes a day, and at most four Sensfrx emails a day in all.
  • Improved: a blocked sign-in sends the customer one email with a reset-password button, not two.
  • Changed: the emails for activity that was allowed (“a login, order or sign-up looked slightly unusual”) are now off. They asked the customer to do nothing. You can switch them back on under Email notifications.
  • Security: someone who has a customer’s password can no longer make your store email that customer a code on every attempt, and the blocked-sign-in message no longer tells them an email was sent.

3.6.1

  • Improved: password-guessing and credential-stuffing protection now counts every failed sign-in correctly. Attempts on made-up usernames count as separate accounts, and a block for guessing one account now takes effect before the password is checked.
  • Privacy: on a failed sign-in the plugin no longer sends the username that was typed. It sends a one-way code made with your store’s secret key, so Sensfrx can count attempts without seeing what was typed (people sometimes type a password into the username box).

3.6.0

  • New: AI agents that prove who they are (for example Google’s shopping agent, by signing its requests) are recognised and shown in Fraud review as “Verified AI agent”. This is a label only: the agent is not trusted more, and every other check still runs.
  • New: requests that pretend to be a known AI agent (such as ChatGPT or Google’s agent) but fail the proof are flagged as “AI Agent Impersonation”.
  • The plugin forwards the agent’s signature headers to Sensfrx for checking. They are public values; no personal data is added.

3.5.0

  • New: the card issuer’s address and security-code checks (AVS / CVV) now help score each order. They are read from the payment gateway after payment: Stripe (official and Payment Plugins), Authorize.Net CIM, Braintree, Square, PayPal advanced card processing, Elavon, Chase Paymentech, CyberSource and other gateways that record them on the order. No card data is sent; only whether each check matched.
  • Improved: shipping to a different address no longer counts against an order on its own (gifts, work and family addresses are normal). Sensfrx now looks at whether the buyer is where the card is, and learns which countries are normal for your store.
  • Fixed: digital products (tickets, courses, downloads) were treated as if they shipped somewhere.

3.4.0

  • Security: password guessing and credential stuffing are now stopped in real time. After repeated failed sign-ins from one network or device (or on one account), further attempts are refused before the password is accepted, with the same message whether the password was right or not. An attacker blocked at two stores is blocked at every Sensfrx store for an hour.
  • Security: a sign-in Sensfrx denies is refused before the session is created (it used to sign the visitor in and then out again). The account owner still gets a password reset email.
  • New: a sign-in Sensfrx challenges now asks for a 6-digit code emailed to the account owner before signing in (it used to let the visitor in and only send an email). Works on wp-login.php and the WooCommerce My Account form.
  • Shadow (monitoring) mode, the admin allow list and API timeouts keep the old behaviour: nothing is blocked.

3.3.0

  • Security: signed webhooks with replay protection, REST nonce checks, webhook secret rotation, credentials no longer written to a public debug log
  • New: Fraud intelligence shows why each event was scored, order number and amount, and links held orders straight to Fraud review; filters built for thousands of events
  • New: Fraud review shows why each order was held and handles large queues (priority sort, filters, paging, bulk actions)
  • New: plan usage shows the checks Sensfrx actually counts this month
  • New: block/allow list values are checked before saving (IP, range, email, domain, username)
  • New: Blocks checkout orders are now scored; historical orders sync

short_description: Stop card testing, fake orders, fake accounts and AI-agent fraud on WooCommerce. Fraud risk scores with plain-language reasons.
description:
WooCommerce fraud prevention built around what store owners actually lose money on: card-testing bots, fake orders and fake accounts, stolen-card orders, AI agents used for fraud, and chargebacks you lose even with proof.

We read 245 merchant threads on Reddit and store-owner forums before building it. The most common complaints were chargebacks lost despite proof, card-testing bots and fake accounts. Each section below starts with one of them.

Sensfrx gives every order, sign-up and login on your store a fraud risk score from 0 to 100, with the reasons in plain words. Clear fraud is refused before the payment is taken. Orders in the gray zone wait for your decision. Real customers check out as before.

The problems it solves

“I’m getting hundreds of card-testing attempts and CAPTCHA doesn’t stop them.”
Card-testing bots skip your storefront and hit the checkout directly, so CAPTCHA never sees them. Sensfrx watches the payments themselves: after repeated declines from one browser, network or delivery address, checkout is refused before another order or charge is created. It covers the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page. During an attack, checkout needs a real browser session; returning customers are not affected.

“Thousands of fake accounts, and my email tool bills me for every one.”
Scripted sign-ups, throwaway email addresses and accounts made in bulk from one device or network are caught at sign-up. Addresses Sensfrx judged fake are kept out of MailPoet, Mailchimp for WooCommerce, Klaviyo, Omnisend, CartFlows and Abandoned Cart Lite, so you stop paying for bot contacts and your abandoned-cart emails stop hurting your sender reputation.

“The order looks risky. Do I ship it or cancel it?”
You get a score with the reasons, not just a label: “4 cards tried in 18 minutes”, “Ships to a parcel forwarder”, “Card used by 3 other customers”. Risky orders go on hold in one Fraud review list, highest risk first, and you approve or cancel in one click.

“I lost the chargeback even though I had proof.”
When an order is disputed as fraud, Sensfrx lists the customer’s earlier undisputed orders from your store that share the same device, IP address or account, and checks them against the Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0, Mastercard and American Express rules. Print it or save it as PDF and attach it to your reply. Customers with an earlier fraud dispute at your store are flagged before you ship again.

“Stolen-card orders keep shipping.”
Every order is scored before you fulfill it, using signals merchants trust: several cards tried on one account, a card shared across customers, many customers ordering from one device, a parcel forwarder. Address (AVS) and security-code (CVV) results from Stripe, Braintree, Square, Authorize.Net, PayPal and other gateways are part of the score.

“I’m paying fees on orders I cancel as fraud.”
Clear fraud is refused before the payment is taken, so there is nothing to refund and no fee kept on a cancelled order.

“AI agents are browsing and checking out on my store. Which ones are fraud?”
AI agents can now browse, sign up and check out like a person, and fraudsters use the same tools to run stolen cards, create accounts and claim coupons at scale. Sensfrx flags sessions that click, move and pause like an AI agent or a scripted browser, and checkouts driven by automation tools such as Playwright, Selenium and Puppeteer. A request that claims to be a known agent, such as ChatGPT’s or Google’s, but fails the proof (a wrong or reused signature, or an address outside the operator’s published ranges) is caught as an impersonator. Agents that prove who they are are labeled “Verified AI agent”, but they are not trusted more: every other check still runs.

Also included

  • Fraud intelligence: every check with its reason. Search by email, IP address or order, filter by risk and export to CSV.
  • 74 fraud rules you control: set the score or action for each, and keep your own block and allow lists by IP address, email, user ID or username.
  • Account protection: logins and password resets from a new device, an unusual network or an impossible location are challenged.

Why store owners trust it

  • Free to start. The Free plan includes 500 checks a month. You add a card to activate it, and the Free plan is not charged.
  • Your checkout never waits on us. If Sensfrx does not answer in time, the order goes through and is marked as not checked.
  • No emails to your customers. Sensfrx never emails your shoppers. Confirmation emails, if you switch them on, go out from your store’s own address.
  • No card data. Card numbers are never sent to Sensfrx.
  • Independently audited. Sensfrx security controls are audited to SOC 2 Type II.

Set up in a minute

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Sensfrx, enter your email and the 6-digit code we send you. No API keys to copy.
  3. Orders, sign-ups and logins are scored from that moment.

“I was being attacked by bots trying to create accounts, but they were very supportive and helpful. I ended up switching to a paid plan because there were so many attacks, but it was worth it. I plan to continue using them.”
Shohei Tanaka, store owner

Privacy & External Services

Important: This plugin connects to Sensfrx.ai (SFX)’s external fraud detection API to provide real-time fraud analysis. When the plugin is active and your store is connected, the following data may be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai servers for fraud detection purposes:

Data Transmitted:

  • User IP addresses and device fingerprints
  • Registration information (email addresses, usernames, registration timestamps)
  • Login attempts, timestamps, and authentication events
  • Transaction details (order amounts, product information, payment methods)
  • User profile updates and password change events
  • Billing and shipping addresses
  • WooCommerce order metadata

External Services Used:

  • Sensfrx.ai (SFX) API: https://sensfrx.ai
  • Privacy Policy: https://sensfrx.ai/privacy-policy
  • Terms of Service: https://sensfrx.ai/terms
  • Trust & Security: https://sensfrx.ai/trust

User Consent & Configuration:

By connecting your store (with your email and a one-time code, or with a Property ID and Property Secret from https://client.sensfrx.ai), you acknowledge that user data will be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai’s servers for fraud analysis. The plugin will not transmit any data until the store is connected.

Data Security:

Sensfrx.ai (SFX) security controls are independently audited (SOC 2 Type II). All data transmissions use HTTPS encryption. For complete details about data handling, retention policies, and your rights under GDPR and other privacy regulations, please review Sensfrx.ai’s Privacy Policy.

Account:

To use this plugin you need a Sensfrx.ai (SFX) account. The plugin creates one when you connect with your email, or you can sign up at https://client.sensfrx.ai/signup. The Free plan includes 500 checks a month; a card is needed to activate it and the Free plan is not charged.

Upgrade Your Store Security

Stop losing revenue to fraud and protect your WooCommerce store with AI-driven fraud detection today!

Get Started for FREE

Support

Join our community for real-time support and fraud prevention insights:

  • Discord: https://discord.gg/zGBGQdwT4r
  • Documentation: Sensfrx WooCommerce Plugin Guide
